num_customers: <int> Number of customers to be visited.
vehicle_capacity: <int> Maximum total demand that a single vehicle can carry on one route.

depot.x: <float> Horizontal coordinate of the depot on the Euclidean grid.
depot.y: <float> Vertical coordinate of the depot on the Euclidean grid.
depot.demand: <int> Goods to be collected at the depot (always zero).
depot.ready_time: <int> Earliest time a vehicle may depart from the depot.
depot.due_date: <int> Latest time by which all vehicles must return to the depot.
depot.service_time: <int> Time spent servicing at the depot (always zero).

customers.id: <int> Unique identifier for the customer, numbered 1 through num_customers.
customers.x: <float> Horizontal coordinate of the customer on the Euclidean grid.
customers.y: <float> Vertical coordinate of the customer on the Euclidean grid.
customers.demand: <int> Quantity of goods to be collected from this customer.
customers.ready_time: <int> Earliest time at which a vehicle may depart from this customer.
customers.due_date: <int> Latest time by which a vehicle must depart from this customer.
customers.service_time: <int> Time a vehicle spends serving this customer before it can depart.

distance_matrix: <list[list[float]], shape [num_customers+1][num_customers+1]> Euclidean distance between each pair of locations, where row/column 0 is the depot and rows/columns 1 through num_customers correspond to customers.
scheduling_horizon: <int> End of the planning period within which all routes must be completed.
travel_time_includes_service_time: <bool> Whether the distance matrix already incorporates each customer's service time into outbound travel times.
primary_objective: <str> The first-priority goal for the optimization.
secondary_objective: <str> The second-priority goal for the optimization, applied as a tiebreaker.
